newsitem.title: USA: Walgreen posts record results, to open 230 stores.
newsitem.headline: Walgreen posts record results, to open 230 stores.

text.p: Walgreen Co. Monday reported record first-quarter results and said it expects to open a record 230 new Walgreens drugstores by the end of August.

Walgreen's profits jumped 18 percent to $75 million, or 30 cents a share, in the first quarter ended Nov. 30, from $63.7 million, or 26 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Revenues grew 13.4 percent to $3.1 billion from $2.7 billion.

The Deerfield, Ill.-based company said earnings were boosted by good control of expenses and strong pharmacy sales, which grew 17.5 percent for the quarter and 11.5 percent in stores open at least a year. Total comparable store sales advanced 8 percent for the quarter.

"We're projecting a record 230 new Walgreens to open this year," Walgreen President L. Daniel Jorndt said in a statement. "Most of these will come in the second half of the year, which is the optimum building season across the country."
Jorndt said Walgreen opened 58 new stores during the first quarter. Sixteen of these were moves to more convenient, freestanding locations that typically generate higher sales and profits, he added.
"By the year 2001 -- our 100th anniversary -- our average Walgreens will be only 5.7 years old -- compared to our average store age of 14.2 years in 1986," Jorndt said.
As of Dec. 31, Walgreen operated 2,238 drug stores in 34 states and Puerto Rico, up from 2,117 a year ago.
Walgreen's stock was unchanged at $40.125 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
